text:
Jackson Independent School District had 4 Asian students in 2024-25
M. S. Weaver
There were four Asian students enrolled in Jackson Independent School District schools in the 2024-25 school year, a 20% decline from the previous year, according to the Kentucky Department of Education.
Data showed that Jackson Independent School District enrolled 392 students in the 2024-25 school year. Asian students accounted for 1% of the student body, the second least represented ethnicity in the district.
Jackson Independent School District covers roughly one school within Breathitt County and keeps its main office in Jackson.
Public school enrollment in Kentucky has not fully recovered from pandemic-era declines. Federal data show enrollment in the state fell by about 5% between fall 2019 and fall 2020, and while some recovery followed, student counts have remained below pre-pandemic levels in recent years.
Kentucky schools continue to face teacher staffing challenges, though recent data show some improvement. The Kentucky Department of Education reported 671 certified teacher vacancies statewide as of Sept. 1, 2025; 34 districts reported having no unfilled certified, classified or licensed positions, up from one district the previous year. The department also found that 72% of districts had seen a decline in qualified applicants over the previous two years.
| Year | Total District Enrollment | Total Asian Students | Asian % |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-25 | 392 | 4 | 1% |
| 2023-24 | 384 | 5 | 1.3% |
| 2022-23 | 369 | 4 | 1.1% |
| 2021-22 | 347 | 5 | 1.4% |
| 2020-21 | 346 | 5 | 1.4% |
| 2019-20 | 354 | 5 | 1.4% |
Information in this article was obtained from the Kentucky Department of Education. The source data are available here.
